full_judgment: 3. Mr. M. H. Khondkar contended that according to the plaint Case the plaintiff himself is to pay Tk. 30,000/- to the defendant for return of the car. The defendant is not liable for any money to the plaintiff. If the plaintiff succeeds in his suit he will get back the car and the defendant will get the money said to have been deposited in Court. In such circumstances the law does not require the defendant to furnish any security. Reference was made to several provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, namely, sections 32(d), 55(4), 60 and 145; and Orders 21, rule 26(3), 32 rule 6, 37 rule 3(2), 38,41 rule 5(3) (c) and 45 rule 7(1)(a) to show the circumstances under which a Court can demand security from a party in a suit and also to show that there was no such circumstances in the present case. So the learned Subordinate Judge had no jurisdiction under the provisions of the Code to direct the defendant in the instant case to furnish security. He tried to impress upon us that the learned Subordinate Judge being conscious of the limitation of his power and jurisdiction assumed jurisdiction to so direct on the consent of the defendant's lawyer or of the defendant herself.
